facts.external_validation: Evaluation using a relevant dataset not used in model development
facts.target_population: The evaluation dataset should represent the intended population, setting and measurement process
facts.clinical_utility: Net benefit weighs potential benefits and harms of a defined action at relevant probability thresholds; decision curves compare alternative strategies
facts.threshold_selection: Relevant thresholds should be chosen before utility analysis with clinical and patient input
facts.calibration: Slope is interpreted alongside other calibration measures and plots, not as proof of reliable individual probabilities

studies.limits: No net benefit calculation, threshold optimization, probability recalibration, prospective impact study or clinical action is performed here

own_study_claims.claim: Fusion OOF AUC rounds to 0.782 and descriptive pooled calibration slope to 0.667; probabilities were not recalibrated
Fusion-minus-M1 paired Brier and logarithmic-loss conditional intervals include zero
At 0.5, 130/141 tumor and 12/41 treatment-change examinations correctly classified; 29 treatment-change classified tumor; accuracy142/182 versus141/182 always-tumor
No action-specific net-benefit study, independent probability recalibration, clinician comparison or downstream clinical outcome evaluation was conducted

interpretations: Observed ranking does not establish reliable individual probabilities or clinical benefit
Fixed-threshold errors identify a limitation but do not show all thresholds would fail or quantify downstream harm
Cross-zero probability-error increments do not prove equivalence or no improvement
A clinically justified action and thresholds would be needed before a clinical utility study; no new threshold recommended
Current evidence supports further evaluation of an incremental imaging signal, not improved outcomes from model-guided care
